content.title: How to vote for Pensacola's Keyla Richardson tonight on 'American Idol'
content.text: March 23, 2026Updated March 24, 2026, 10:41 a.m. CTPensacola native Keyla Richardson is competing for a spot in the "American Idol" Top 14Fans can vote for Richardson via the show's website, text message, or social media platformsRichardson secured her place in the Top 20 after successfully passing through the show's Ohana Round in HawaiiThe "American Idol" Top 14 will be revealed on the March 30 episode based on America's votesPensacola’s very own Keyla Richardson performs tonight for her chance to enter the American Idol Top 14, and voting is now open to help get her there.Voting starts at the beginning of the broadcast at 7 p.m. CT, and the voting window will remain open until 5 a.m. CT on March 24.How to vote for Keyla Richardson on American IdolThere are three ways to vote on American Idol — on the American Idol website, over text message, and the newly introduced social media voting method, using Facebook, Instagram and TikTok.Each week, voters may vote 10 times per contestant per method, so each person could cast 50 votes for Richardson across all methods.For voting on the American Idol website, visit AmericanIdol.com/Vote once the voting window opens.For text message voting, text the number of the finalist you would like to vote for to “21523.” Richardson’s voting number will be 20.How American Idol’s new social media voting worksIn order to make the most of American Idol’s new social voting, there are some ground rules to understand.Voters need to visit American Idol’s “Official Vote Post,” which will be pinned on each platform, then leave a comment on the post that includes who they are voting for. You can vote up to 10 times per contestant per platform, but all votes must be cast in individual comments.Voters cannot include the names of multiple contestants in one comment, or repeat the name of the same contestant multiple times in one comment.To view the full guidance on voting, visit idolvote.abc.com/#faq.Where was Keyla Richardson in last week’s episode?This month, Richardson successfully passed through the show’s new Ohana Round at Disney’s Aulani Resort in Hawaii, securing her space in the Top 20. The remaining contestants performed again in Hawaii, this time for America's votes rather than the judges'. Their performances were aired in two parts, on March 16 and March 23, as pre-recorded episodes. Since Richardson’s performance didn’t air until March 23, her voting window didn’t open until the beginning of this week’s episode.Richardson attended a watch party for the episode last week at Andy D’s on Pensacola Bay with her 9-year-old son, Drew, where she was surrounded by family, friends and fans cheering her on in her American Idol journey.What’s next on American Idol?After hearing all of the Top 20’s performances split across two episodes, starting on March 16 (Episode 8) and concluding on March 23 (Episode 9), America's votes will determine the singers' fate for the Top 14, which will be revealed on the March 30 episode.How to watch season 24 of American IdolABC airs American Idol at 7 p.m. CDT every Monday. If you don't have cable, paid streaming platforms also show episodes in real time, such as YouTube TV, DirecTV, Fubo, Sling, Hulu + Live TV and more. If you missed it, the episode is then available to stream on Hulu the next day.Who’s in the American Idol Top 20?These are the singers who made the American Idol Top 20 for 2026:Jordan McCullough (platinum ticket)Brooks Rosser (platinum ticket)Kyndal Inskeep (platinum ticket)Keyla RichardsonRuby RaeMadison MoonPhilmon LeeBraden RumfeltJake ThistleJesse FindlingGenevieve HeywardLucas LeonHannah HarperChris TungsethJulián KalelRaeDaniel StallworthAbayomiKutter BradleyMakiyahKeyla Richardson’s road to the Top 20Richardson received her coveted golden ticket on "American Idol" after an emotional audition on the Season 24 premiere on Jan. 26, even bringing Bryan to tears with her soulful rendition of “Glitter in the Air” by P!nk. After three unanimous “yes” votes, the judges gave her the green light, clearing her way to Hollywood week.“The audition process, it was a lot. It was very tedious. I was a nervous wreck,” Richardson told the News Journal. “My mind was everywhere. I was just ready to audition…you have to wait around, so many people ahead of you. Early mornings, it was a lot. I pushed through because this is what I wanted to do and I wanted it to work out.”Since Richardson’s audition was aired in episode one, Richardson wasn’t on-screen again until the start of Hollywood Week on Feb. 23, nearly a month after her debut.There, Richardson continued to wow the judges, earning a standing ovation from her rendition of “I Won’t Give Up” by Jason Mraz.Richardson’s performance earned her temporary safety in the American Idol Golden Room, exempting her from an initial round of cuts from the judges. The episode ended on a cliffhanger, leaving Richardson waiting with the other Golden Room recipients to learn whether she had landed a place in the show’s coveted Top 30. However, she has had to work hard to get there.“The biggest challenge is just the early mornings and the late nights. As an artist, this is something that we have to do,” Richardson said. “I had to really just adjust to having to move and do things even when I’m tired…this is what I signed up for, it’s what I wanted to do. So, that’s been the hardest part, but now, I’m adjusting. I’m good now.”Richardson’s musical journey started in PensacolaRichardson has been singing almost her entire life, starting with singing gospel in Pensacola's churches.“I’ve always had a love for singing. I’ve been singing since the age of 5. I was raised in the church and so I just wanted to do more,” Richardson said. “I felt like I was just in a box and I just wanted to branch out and see what they got in store for me.”She went on to become a music teacher at Life Shifting Learning Academy on Pensacola Boulevard, where she’s been for about six years. She knows what it’s like to need someone to believe in you, and also importantly, to learn to believe in yourself. Now, she works to help young people develop their voices and gets to be the one who believes in them.Now, when Richardson visits her students during the season, she is able to pass along lots of hugs and a few words of wisdom.“They hug on me, love on me. I have to make them do their work,” Richardson said of her students. “I just want to let the world know, never give up. Always chase your dream, don’t let nobody stop you chasing your dream. You just keep going, no matter what.”What is American Idol about?American Idol is a series known for “pioneering the music competition genre,” according to the American Idol website. The show features celebrity judges, including Carrie Underwood, a fourth-season American Idol winner. This year, Underwood joined judges Luke Bryan and Lionel Richie to listen to auditions across all genres as they assemble a group of competitors to move forward, with America determining their fate. The show is hosted by Ryan Seacrest, and while judges have come and gone, Seacrest has been with Idol since its 2002 debut.
